## Body

Output publication permission is not request-answer authority.

PM's explicit PR #137 ruling allows a flagged non-holder to publish an output. Using --answers to finalize a request or trigger its associated forced wake instead requires the writer to be the request's recorded holder, a live holder of its role, or that request project's prime.

Resolve these authorities from the stored request, not the output's declared context or its writer_holds_role flag. A project creator is not automatically its prime. A recorded holder remains independently permitted; do not replace the three-case rule with current-holder-only access.

Refuse an ineligible --answers operation by name before any writer commit, stamp or notification. Explain the next step: get assigned or write without --answers. Do not silently downgrade an unauthorized answer into a published output.

The blocked snapshot 4ab6460fc70d4d0cf9dda07910d9664fb4f8546a has a passing CI test where the writer is the project creator but outside all three authorities; the handler still stamps answered_at and admits notification. The fake-ddocs HTTP test demonstrates state/notification admission, not a live cold-session wake. A mandatory cold audit is necessary but does not supply missing answer authorization.

That snapshot's external links have no scheme/control allowlist, but no own-code fetch/autolaunch was found. Do not upgrade this into demonstrated SSRF/XSS without a consumption path; real renderer safety remained unproved.
